subject: Optimize toolkit: structuring credits + quantization play for FinInsight
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@fininsight.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <contracts@procureops.com>, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@fininsight.com>
Date: 2026-10-04 09:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize trial summary + next steps

Hi Marcus / Lauren,

Thanks again for the trial summary you sent last week. Our exec sponsor (Carlos) asked for one consolidated commercial proposal that maps the Optimizer recommendations (batching + KV caching + 4-bit quantization) to expected monthly run rates for our 3 workloads.

Our procurement team also wanted clarity on:
- How credits would be consumed vs. committed monthly capacity,
- What discount tiers are available for quantized models vs. FP16,
- Whether Redwood can guarantee no performance regressions if we adopt the 4-bit profile for the latency-sensitive path.

We attached a rough SOW and our expected traffic pattern. Can you provide a short options grid (3 options: conservative / balanced / aggressive) with pricing and a recommended migration path? We need this to make the Q4 procurement cut.

Thanks,
Emma
FinInsight — Director, Platform

Attachments: FinInsight_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (pdf), traffic_sample.csv (csv)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@fininsight.com>, ProcureOps <contracts@procureops.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize trial summary + next steps

Hi Emma — really appreciate the clear asks. High level response first, detailed grid next: 

TL;DR: We can present three commercial options that reflect increasing use of caching + quantization. All options include the Optimize toolkit license and 30 days of onboarding support. We recommend the balanced option for FinInsight as it reduces token spend by ~35% vs baseline with minimal latency impact.

Action: Ill pull together the option grid and include expected unit economics. Copying Lauren and Ben for procurement/pricing validation. Ill aim to send the grid plus a redline SOW by EOD tomorrow.

Quick clarifications for your procurement team:
- Credits vs committed capacity: credits are consumed by generated tokens (post-batching). Committed capacity buys predictable baseline throughput and reduces per-token unit cost; we can structure the commit to include a credits allowance that rolls month-to-month.
- Discounts for quantized models: we offer a quantization differential (typically 10–25% depending on volume and model family). We can attach a firm discount tier once we confirm expected token volumes.
- Performance regressions: our Optimize quality checks include a holdout eval set and rollback policy; any 4-bit profile is validated on your latency/quality guardrails before production rollout.

Will follow up with the three-option grid.

—Marcus
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Schedule a quick follow-up: https://calendly.com/marcus-redwood/30

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04 14:21 -0700
Subject: Internal: FinInsight pricing ask (need concession guidance)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding FinInsight request. They want a 3-option grid. Two items where I may need your call:

1) They will likely ask for an upfront credit commitment with a 12-month term. They're signalling wanting a 20% blended discount if we include the quantized profiles in the commit. Can we go to 18% on sticker for the balanced option if they commit $150k/month?
2) They asked if we can guarantee no performance regressions on the latency-sensitive path with 4-bit. We do run rollout checks, but procurement is pushing for an SLA-like clause or a short trial period as acceptance criteria. Are we comfortable adding an acceptance window (30 days post-rollout) with a remediation credit if quality delta > agreed threshold?

I included the draft SOW and the quantization profile sheet from R&D (attached). Happy to hop on a quick call.

—Marcus

Attachments: Quant_Profile_Sheet.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04 15:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: FinInsight pricing ask (need concession guidance)

Thanks Marcus — quick guidance: 
- Discount: approve up to 18% net on the balanced option for a 12-month $150k/month commit, provided we keep the full list price on non-committed overage and include an annual price review.
- Acceptance/quality window: approve a 30-day acceptance window with remediation credits capped at 10% of the first months invoice, not cumulative. Remediation should be measured against the holdout eval suite they provided. Legal can draft a short acceptance appendix.

Ben — please prepare the pricing table with the margin impact and a fallback of a lower-commit tier (90k/month) at a smaller discount (10%).

Marissa
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@fininsight.com>, ProcureOps <contracts@procureops.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05 09:08 -0700
Subject: Optimize options for FinInsight — conservative / balanced / aggressive

Emma / Carlos / Contracts — attached is the three-option commercial grid and an updated SOW redline. Summary below (details in attachments):

1) Conservative — Minimal changes (no quantization), smaller commit, higher per-token cost. Good if you want zero-risk.
2) Balanced (recommended) — 12-month $150k/month commit, includes Optimize toolkit license, KV/prefix caching defaults, and 4-bit quantization for non-latency critical paths. Pricing: 18% net discount on units inside commit, overage at list. Acceptance: 30-day post-rollout validation using FinInsight holdout eval; remediation credit capped at 10% of month 1 invoice.
3) Aggressive — larger commit ($250k/month) with broader quantization across workloads, higher saving (25%+), but requires an initial 2-week joint tuning engagement.

Attachments: FinInsight_SOW_draft_v2.pdf, Quant_Profile_Sheet.xlsx

Next steps: If procurement likes the balanced option, can ProcureOps send a PO to contracts@redwood.com and we will issue a DocuSign SOW. If you want us to tighten the acceptance appendix wording before PO, we can loop legal.

—Marcus
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: FinInsight_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (pdf), Quant_Profile_Sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

From: ProcureOps <contracts@procureops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@fininsight.com>, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@fininsight.com>
Date: 2026-10-07 17:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize options for FinInsight — conservative / balanced / aggressive

Marcus / Marissa — thanks for the options. FinInsight will proceed with the balanced option conditional on:
- A 12-month PO at $150k/month to be submitted next week,
- The acceptance appendix included in the DocuSign SOW,
- A 30-day ramp period to validate the 4-bit profiles on our staging cluster, with the remediation credit and the measurement suite as you described.

Please send the DocuSign link for the SOW and we will route the PO. Also include the billing contact details and a single point of contact for onboarding.

Thanks,
Contracts Desk
FinInsight

DocuSign request: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ZZY123-fininsight-sow
